### Population trajectory without management

```{r}
#| label: fig-trajectory
#| fig-cap: "Figure shows the change in median wild pig density relative to the initial median density at week 0 over a one-year period. The boxplots represent the median and interquartile range (IQR) of these changes, where the whiskers extend plus or minus 1.5 times the IQR with outliers removed. The Without management scenario (orange) is the result of the boostrapping procedure (see methods section ##), and the With managment scenario (purple) compares median posterior density estimates. The rows represent the density category at week 0, where Low is less than 2 pigs/km2, Medium is between 2-6 pigs/km2, and High is greater than 6 pigs/km2. Note the different y-axis scale for each initial density category."

tar_read("plot_management")

```

```{r}
#| label: bootstap analysis
df <- tar_read("bootstrap_mgmt")

md <- max(df$delta_time)

cat_medians <- df |>
  filter(
    delta_time == md
  ) |>
  group_by(st_name, density_cat, mgmt) |>
  summarise(
    med = round(median(delta_density), 1),
    low = round(quantile(delta_density, 0.05), 1),
    high = round(quantile(delta_density, 0.95), 1)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(u = paste0("90% CI: ", low, "-", high))

get_median_changes <- function(df, dc, mc, s) {
  df |>
    filter(
      density_cat == dc,
      mgmt == mc,
      st_name == s
    ) |>
    pull(med)
}

get_u <- function(df, dc, mc, s) {
  df |>
    filter(
      density_cat == dc,
      mgmt == mc,
      st_name == s
    ) |>
    pull(u)
}

tx_m_high_wo <- cat_medians |> get_median_changes("High", "Without", "TEXAS")
tx_m_high_w <- cat_medians |> get_median_changes("High", "With", "TEXAS")
tx_u_high_wo <- cat_medians |> get_u("High", "Without", "TEXAS")
tx_u_high_w <- cat_medians |> get_u("High", "With", "TEXAS")
tx_diff <- tx_m_high_wo - tx_m_high_w

delta_density <- cat_medians |>
  select(st_name, density_cat, mgmt, med) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = mgmt, values_from = med) |>
  mutate(delta = Without - With)

min_delta <- delta_density |>
  group_by(density_cat) |>
  filter(delta == min(delta))
max_delta <- delta_density |>
  group_by(density_cat) |>
  filter(delta == max(delta))

get_delta <- function(df, x, c) {
  df |>
    filter(density_cat == x) |>
    pull(all_of(c))
}

min_low_delta_m <- get_delta(min_delta, "Low", "delta")
min_med_delta_m <- get_delta(min_delta, "Medium", "delta")
min_high_delta_m <- get_delta(min_delta, "High", "delta")
min_low_delta_s <- get_delta(min_delta, "Low", "st_name")
min_med_delta_s <- get_delta(min_delta, "Medium", "st_name")
min_high_delta_s <- get_delta(min_delta, "High", "st_name")

max_low_delta_m <- get_delta(max_delta, "Low", "delta")
max_med_delta_m <- get_delta(max_delta, "Medium", "delta")[1]
max_high_delta_m <- get_delta(max_delta, "High", "delta")[1]
max_low_delta_s <- get_delta(max_delta, "Low", "st_name")
max_med_delta_s <- get_delta(max_delta, "Medium", "st_name")[1]
max_high_delta_s <- get_delta(max_delta, "High", "st_name")[1]

n_below_0 <- df |>
  filter(delta_density < 0, delta_time == md) |>
  group_by(mgmt, density_cat) |>
  summarise(n_below_0 = n())

n_all <- df |>
  filter(delta_time == md) |>
  group_by(mgmt, density_cat) |>
  summarise(n = n())

pfall <- left_join(n_all, n_below_0) |>
  mutate(percent_fell = round(n_below_0 / n * 100, 1))

get_p <- function(x, c) {
  pfall |>
    filter(
      density_cat == x,
      mgmt == c
    ) |>
    pull(percent_fell)
}

p_w_l <- get_p("Low", "With")
p_wo_l <- get_p("Low", "Without")
p_w_m <- get_p("Medium", "With")
p_wo_m <- get_p("Medium", "Without")
p_w_h <- get_p("High", "With")
p_wo_h <- get_p("High", "Without")


```

The effect of pig removals was more evident when the initial density was high (i.e. \> 6 pigs/km2), and varied across states regardless of initial density (@fig-trajectory). In Texas, for example, there was no change in pig density after one year when the initial density was low (i.e. \< 2 pigs/km2), regardless if management (i.e. pig removals) occurred or not. However, when management occurred and initial density was high, the median change in density after one year was `r tx_m_high_w` (`r tx_u_high_w`), where as the predicted change in density if management did not occur was `r tx_m_high_wo` (`r tx_u_high_wo`). That means that after one year high density properties in Texas that did not conduct pig removals could have wild pig densities that are `r tx_diff` pigs/km2 higher than properties that removed pigs.

The variation in the effect of management across states increased with each density category. When the initial density was low, the difference between conducting removals and not was between `r min_low_delta_m` and `r max_low_delta_m` pigs/km2 after one year in `r min_low_delta_s` and `r max_low_delta_s`, respectively. When the initial density was between 2-6 pigs/km2 (i.e. medium), the difference between conducting removals and not was between `r min_med_delta_m` and `r max_med_delta_m` pigs/km2 after one year in `r min_med_delta_s` and `r max_med_delta_s`, respectively. When the initial density was high, the difference between conducting removals and not was between `r min_high_delta_m` and `r max_high_delta_m` pigs/km2 after one year in `r min_high_delta_s` and `r max_high_delta_s`, respectively.

Across all bootstrap simulations, `r p_w_l`, `r p_w_m`, and `r p_w_h`percent of properties saw wild pig densities fall after one year while conducting removals for the low, medium, and high initial density scenarios, respectively. This is in contrast to the simulations that did not conduct removals, where `r p_wo_l`, `r p_wo_m`, and `r p_wo_h`percent of properties saw wild pig densities fall after one year for the low, medium, and high initial density scenarios, respectively.

### Population growth rate

```{r}
#| label: fig-lambda
#| fig-cap: "Figure shows the average population growth rate at each property within each state. The number of properties (n) within each state are on the y-axis. A growth rate greater than one indicates that a property's population is growing. Values of zero represent properties that went extinct between the first and second observed primary periods. Boxplots represent the median and interquartile range (IQR), where the whiskers extend plus or minus 1.5 times the IQR."

tar_read("plot_lambda_hat_by_state")

```

```{r}
#| label: lambda analysis

df <- tar_read("mu_lambda")

all_prop_med <- round(median(df$mu), 2)
all_prop_low <- round(quantile(df$mu, 0.05), 2)
all_prop_high <- round(quantile(df$mu, 0.95), 2)

n_props <- nrow(df)
n_declining <- df |>
  filter(mu < 1) |>
  nrow()
percent_declining <- round(n_declining / n_props * 100)

lambda_summary <- df |>
  group_by(st_name) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    med = median(mu),
    mu_hat = mean(mu),
    sd = sd(mu),
    q1 = quantile(mu, 0.25),
    q3 = quantile(mu, 0.75)
  ) |>
  arrange(med)

low <- lambda_summary |>
  filter(med == min(med))
state_low <- low$st_name
low_lambda <- round(low$med, 2)

high <- lambda_summary |>
  filter(med == max(med))
state_high <- high$st_name
high_lambda <- round(high$med, 2)


low_sd <- lambda_summary |>
  filter(sd == min(sd, na.rm = TRUE))
state_low_sd <- low_sd$st_name
low_lambda_sd <- round(low_sd$sd, 2)

high_sd <- lambda_summary |>
  filter(sd == max(sd, na.rm = TRUE))
state_high_sd <- high_sd$st_name
high_lambda_sd <- round(high_sd$sd, 2)

n_under_1 <- lambda_summary |>
  filter(med < 1) |>
  nrow()

n0 <- df |>
  filter(mu == 0) |>
  nrow()

```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-lambda
#| tbl-cap: The mean and standard deviation (SD) of average property growth rates across properties in each state (n is the number of properties in each state).

lambda_summary |>
  rename(
    State = st_name,
    Mean = mu_hat,
    SD = sd
  ) |>
  mutate(Mean = round(Mean, 2), SD = round(SD, 2)) |>
  select(State, Mean, SD, n) |>
  arrange(desc(Mean)) |>
  knitr::kable()

```

Individual properties exhibited a range of average population growth rates in the presence of removal activities. Across all properties the median population growth rate per 28-day period was `r all_prop_med` (90% CI: `r all_prop_low` - `r all_prop_high`). Meaning just over half (`r percent_declining`%, n=`r n_declining`) of the properties had declining populations, which includes the effect of management activities. There was variation within and across states (@fig-lambda). For example, the median growth rate per 28-day period ranged from `r low_lambda` to `r high_lambda` for `r state_low` and `r state_high`, respectively. Additionaly, there were `r n_under_1` states where at least half of their properties had a declining population (@tbl-lambda). Finally, there were `r n0` properties with a growth rate of zero, which are properties that eradicated wild pigs between their first and second primary periods with removal events.

### Proportion removed

```{r}
#| label: fig-removals
#| fig-cap: "Summary of the avearge proportion of the population removed by method at the property level. Boxplots represent the median and interquartile range (IQR), where the whiskers extend plus or minus 1.5 times the IQR."

```

```{r}
#| label: proportion take
df_actual <- tar_read("actual_percent_take")
df_lambda <- tar_read("mu_lambda") |>
  rename(lambda = mu) |>
  select(-n)

df_epr <- left_join(df_actual, df_lambda) |>
  filter(!is.na(lambda)) |>
  mutate(epr = 1 + (lambda * (mu_prop_take - 1)))

calc_epr <- function(lambda, apr) 1 + (lambda * (apr - 1))

calc_epr(1, 0.5)
calc_epr(1, 1)
calc_epr(0.5, 0.5)
calc_epr(2, 1)
calc_epr(1.5, 0.25)

epr_by_st_method <- df_epr |>
  group_by(st_name, method) |>
  summarise(
    med = round(median(epr), 2),
    low = round(quantile(epr, 0.05), 2),
    high = round(quantile(epr, 0.95), 2)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

tx_epr_heli <- epr_by_st_method |>
  filter(method == "Helicopter", st_name == "TEXAS")
tx_epr_heli_med <- tx_epr_heli$med
tx_epr_heli_low <- tx_epr_heli$low
tx_epr_heli_high <- tx_epr_heli$high

by_state <- function(df) {
  df |>
    group_by(method, st_name) |>
    summarise(
      med = median(mu_prop_take),
      low = quantile(mu_prop_take, 0.05),
      high = quantile(mu_prop_take, 0.95)
    ) |>
    ungroup()
}

a_by_state <- by_state(df_actual)

tx_heli <- a_by_state |>
  filter(method == "Helicopter", st_name == "TEXAS")

tx_heli_med <- round(tx_heli$med, 2)
tx_heli_low <- round(tx_heli$low, 2)
tx_heli_high <- round(tx_heli$high, 2)

get_example <- function(x, g) {
  round(-1 * (1 - g) / (x - 1), 2)
}

tx_0 <- get_example(tx_heli_med, 0)
tx_0.5 <- get_example(tx_heli_med, 0.5)

tx_lambda <- lambda_summary |>
  filter(st_name == "TEXAS")
tx_lambda_med <- tx_lambda$med

# p_lower_0 <- round(pnorm(tx_0, tx_lambda_mu, tx_lambda_sd) * 100, 1)
# p_lower_0.5 <- round(pnorm(tx_0.5, tx_lambda_mu, tx_lambda_sd) * 100, 1)

epr <- function(apr, lambda) {
  1 + (lambda * (apr - 1))
}

tx_heli_epr <- epr(tx_heli_med, tx_lambda_med)


```

Here, we focus on the proportion of the population removed by method and state (@fig-removals A), which must be interpreted with respect to population growth rate (@fig-removals B). 
For example, in Texas the median proportion of the population removed (APR) in a single primary period by helicopters was `r tx_heli_med` (90% CI `r tx_heli_low` - `r tx_heli_high`; @fig-removals A). 
Given the distribution of growth rates across properties in Texas, the EPR of helicopters in Texas was `r tx_epr_heli_med` (90% CI `r tx_epr_heli_low` - `r tx_epr_heli_high`). 



```{r}
#| label: tbl-aprEpr
#| tbl-cap: "The actual proportion of the population removed (APR) and the effective proportion of the population remove (EPR) across properties that used each method in each state. Negative EPR indicates the population is expected to grow. The units represent the distribution of APR and EPR given the number of properties (n) that used the method in each state. For one property we show the single value, between two and ten properties we show the range, and for ten or more properties we show the median and 90% confidence interval."

df_epr |>
  select(method, st_name, mu_prop_take, epr) |>
  rename(APR = mu_prop_take, EPR = epr) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(APR, EPR), names_to = "metric") |>
  group_by(method, st_name, metric) |>
  summarise(
    med = round(median(value), 2),
    low = round(quantile(value, 0.05), 2),
    high = round(quantile(value, 0.95), 2),
    min = round(min(value), 2),
    max = round(max(value), 2),
    n = n()
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    dist = if_else(n == 1, as.character(med), paste0("[", min, "-", max, "]")),
    Units = if_else(n == 1, "Value", "Range"),
    dist = if_else(n >= 10, paste0(med, " (", low, "-", high, ")"), dist),
    Units = if_else(n >= 10, "Median (90% C.I.)", Units)
  ) |>
  select(-med, -low, -high, -min, -max) |>
  distinct() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = dist) |>
  rename(State = st_name, Method = method) |>
  select(State, Method, APR, EPR, Units, n) |>
  arrange(State, Method) |>
  knitr::kable()


```

Lastly, for helicopters, the range in the median proportion of the populatino removed was between `r round(heli_min$med, 2)` (90% CI: `r round(heli_min$low, 2)` - `r round(heli_min$high, 2)`) and `r round(heli_max$med, 2)` (90% CI: `r round(heli_max$low, 2)` - `r round(heli_max$high, 2)`) for `r heli_min$st_name` and `r heli_max$st_name`, respectively.



```{r}
#| label: fig-epr
#| fig-cap: A) The average actual proportion of the population removed (APR) by each method in each property. B) The area of each property where methods where used. C) The average total effort per unit deployed for each method in each property. D) The theoretical expected proportion of the population remaining (EPR) given growth rate and APR. A value of 1 indicates eradication, 0 indicates no change, and -1 indicates a populattion expected to double. The dashed line shos the threshold at which populations are expected to grow or increase, and the dotted line shows the threshold at which populations are expected to reduce by more (slash) or less (shrink) than half. For A-C, the data are grouped into the EPR given the average growth rate of the property where the method was deployed. Events the led to population growth are in red, events that lead to a shrinking population are in light blue, and events that lead to a slashing population are in dark blue.

tar_read("plot_epr")

```


```{r}

df <- tar_read("epr_data")

make_epr_summaries <- function(df, y) {
  df |>
    group_by(method, epr_cat) |>
    summarise(
      med = as.character(round(median(.data[[y]]), 2)),
      low = round(quantile(.data[[y]], 0.05), 2),
      high = round(quantile(.data[[y]], 0.95), 2)
    ) |>
    ungroup()
}

aprs <- make_epr_summaries(df, "mu_prop_take")
area <- make_epr_summaries(df, "property_area_km2")
effort <- make_epr_summaries(df, "mu_total_effort_per")

epr_kable <- function(df) {
  df |>
    mutate(value = paste0(med, " (", low, "-", high, ")")) |>
    select(-low, -high, -med) |>
    rename(`EPR` = epr_cat, `Median (90% CI)` = value) |>
    knitr::kable()
}


```

### The expected proportion of the population remaining (EPR)

The expected proportion of the population remaining (EPR) is a metric that combines the actual proportion removed (APR) with the population growth rate to estimate the net effect of removals on population size. If EPR equals 1, the population is expected to be eradicated, at zero the population is expected to remain unchanged, and if less than zero, the population is expected to grow. This metric allows for direct comparison of removal effectiveness across properties and methods. 

As expected, to slash a population (i.e. reduce it by more than half) the APR was greater than to shrink a population (i.e. reduce it by less than half), and the smallest APRs actually resulted in a growing population (@fig-epr A). While this was apparent for all methods, the APR needed to slash a population varied. For example, to slash a popultion with helicopters the APR needed was 5.2 times greater than what was needed to slash the population by traps. Likewise, to shrink a population the helicopters need to take 5.5 times more than what was needed by traps. The APRs resulting in a growing population were small and consistent across methods (Supplement table S##).

There was a gradient in property area where take that was expected to slash a population mostly occurred on smaller properties compared to that of shrinking and growing. This gradient was apparent for all methods (@fig-epr B). For example, the median property size (km^2) where growth was expected to occurr compared to where slashing was expected to occur was on properterites that were 3.4, 1.5, 3.7, 5.2 and 2.9 times larger for traps, snares, sharpshooting, helicopters, and fixed wing aircraft, respectively (Supplement table S##). 

The effort required to achieve a significant reduction in the population was remarkably similar to the effort observed in cases where populations were expected to grow. For example, the largest difference in effort per unit deployed was for sharpshooting, where 5 (90% CI 1.9-20.8) shooters per hour resulted in slashing and 7.83 (90% CI 2.25-22.5) shooters per hour resulted in population growth (Supplementary table s##).

```{r}
epr_kable(aprs)
```

```{r}

calculate_lambda_needed <- function(df, g, prop_rem_col) {
  df |>
    mutate(
      goal = g,
      lambda_needed = (g - 1) / (.data[[prop_rem_col]] - 1),
      lambda_needed = round(lambda_needed, 2)
    )
}

g0_all <- df_actual |> calculate_lambda_needed(0, "mu_prop_take")
g0.5_all <- df_actual |> calculate_lambda_needed(0.5, "mu_prop_take")

g0_all2 <- g0_all |>
  select(propertyID, method, lambda_needed) |>
  rename(lambda_needed_0 = lambda_needed)
g0.5_all2 <- g0.5_all |>
  select(propertyID, method, lambda_needed) |>
  rename(lambda_needed_0.5 = lambda_needed)

all_lambda_needed <- left_join(g0_all2, g0.5_all2)

df_actual_lambda_needed <- left_join(df_actual, all_lambda_needed)

df_property_method <- df_actual |>
  select(propertyID, method) |>
  unique()

df <- tar_read("mu_lambda")

lambda_by_method <- left_join(df_property_method, df) |>
  filter(!is.na(mu)) |>
  rename(lambda_actual = mu)

df_actual_lambda_join <- left_join(df_actual_lambda_needed, lambda_by_method)

lambda_filter <- df_actual_lambda_join |>
  filter(!is.na(lambda_actual)) |>
  mutate(
    maintenance_2_half = if_else(lambda_actual <= lambda_needed_0 &
      lambda_actual > lambda_needed_0.5, TRUE, FALSE),
    half = if_else(lambda_actual <= lambda_needed_0.5, TRUE, FALSE),
    check = if_else(half & maintenance_2_half, FALSE, TRUE)
  )

all(lambda_filter$check)

g0_filter <- left_join(lambda_by_method, g0_all) |>
  filter(lambda_actual <= lambda_needed)
g0.5_filter <- left_join(lambda_by_method, g0.5_all) |>
  filter(lambda_actual <= lambda_needed)

summarise_property <- function(df1, df2) {
  bind_rows(df1, df2) |>
    group_by(method, goal) |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      med_lambda = round(median(lambda_needed), 2),
      low_lambda = round(quantile(lambda_needed, 0.05), 2),
      high_lambda = round(quantile(lambda_needed, 0.95), 2),
      med_prop_take = round(median(mu_prop_take), 2),
      low_prop_take = round(quantile(mu_prop_take, 0.05), 2),
      high_prop_take = round(quantile(mu_prop_take, 0.95), 2),
      med_prop_take = round(median(mu_prop_take), 2),
      low_prop_take = round(quantile(mu_prop_take, 0.05), 2),
      high_prop_take = round(quantile(mu_prop_take, 0.95), 2),
      med_total_effort = round(median(mu_total_effort), 2),
      low_total_effort = round(quantile(mu_total_effort, 0.05), 2),
      high_total_effort = round(quantile(mu_total_effort, 0.95), 2),
      med_total_effort_per = round(median(mu_total_effort_per), 2),
      low_total_effort_per = round(quantile(mu_total_effort_per, 0.05), 2),
      high_total_effort_per = round(quantile(mu_total_effort_per, 0.95), 2),
      med_total_trap_count = round(median(mu_total_trap_count), 2),
      low_total_trap_count = round(quantile(mu_total_trap_count, 0.05), 2),
      high_total_trap_count = round(quantile(mu_total_trap_count, 0.95), 2)
    ) |>
    ungroup()
}

property_stats <- summarise_property(g0_filter, g0.5_filter)

my_paste0 <- function(med, low, high) {
  paste0(med, " (", low, "-", high, ")")
}

all_under_names <- property_stats |>
  mutate(
    Goal = if_else(goal == 0, "Maintenance", "50% reduction"),
    `Growth rate` = my_paste0(
      med_lambda,
      low_lambda,
      high_lambda
    ),
    `Proportion removed` = my_paste0(
      med_prop_take,
      low_prop_take,
      high_prop_take
    ),
    `Effort` = my_paste0(
      med_total_effort,
      low_total_effort,
      high_total_effort
    ),
    `Units deployed` = my_paste0(
      med_total_trap_count,
      low_total_trap_count,
      high_total_trap_count
    ),
    `Effort per unit` = my_paste0(
      med_total_effort_per,
      low_total_effort_per,
      high_total_effort_per
    )
  ) |>
  rename(
    Method = method
  ) |>
  select(Method, Goal, `Proportion removed`, Effort, `Units deployed`, `Effort per unit`, `Growth rate`, n)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-reduceByState

g0 <- a_by_state |> calculate_lambda_needed(0, "med")

lambda_summary_2 <- lambda_summary |>
  select(st_name, mu_hat, sd)

p_under <- bind_rows(g0, g0.5) |>
  left_join(lambda_summary_2) |>
  mutate(percent_under = round(pnorm(lambda_needed, mu_hat, sd) * 100, 1)) |>
  select(method, st_name, percent_under, goal, lambda_needed) |>
  rename(
    lambda = lambda_needed,
    State = st_name,
    Goal = goal
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Goal = if_else(Goal == 0, "Maintenance", "50% reduction"),
    x = paste0(lambda, " (", percent_under, ")")
  ) |>
  select(-percent_under, -lambda)

p_under |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = x) |>
  arrange(State, Goal) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
grid_search <- expand_grid(
  lambda = seq(0.5, 2, by = 0.01),
  goal = c(0, 0.5, 1) # 1 is elimination, zero is no change
) |>
  filter(goal + lambda >= 1) |>
  mutate(needed = -1 * (((1 - goal) - lambda) / lambda))

grid_search |>
  mutate(
    goal_cat = if_else(goal == 0, "Maintenance", "Eradication"),
    goal_cat = if_else(goal == 0.5, "50% reduction", goal_cat),
    goal_cat = factor(goal_cat, levels = c("Maintenance", "50% reduction", "Eradication"))
  ) |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(y = needed, x = lambda, color = goal_cat) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 3) +
  scale_color_viridis_d() +
  labs(
    y = "Proportion of individuals needed to be removed",
    x = "Populuation growth rate per 28-days",
    color = "Management\ngoal"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```         
dat <- tar_read("model_data_last")
dat_take <- dat |>
  group_by(propertyID, end_dates, method) |>
  summarise(
    take = sum(take),
    effort = sum(effort),
    trap_count = sum(trap_count)
  ) |>
  ungroup()

areas <- dat |>
  select(propertyID, property_area_km2) |>
  unique()

df <- tar_read("realized_growth")
glimpse(df)


left_join(df, areas) |>
  filter(abundance_estimate > 0) |>
  mutate(
    density = abundance_estimate / property_area_km2,
    log_density = log(density)
  ) |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = density, y = lambda) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw()

t2 <- df |>
  count(propertyID) |>
  filter(n >= 2) |>
  pull(propertyID)

lambda_tp1 <- df |>
  select(propertyID, end_dates, st_name, total_take, abundance_estimate, lambda)

tmp <- left_join(dat_take, lambda_tp1) |>
  filter(!is.na(lambda)) |>
  mutate(
    percent_take = take / abundance_estimate,
    log_take_p1 = log(take + 1),
    log_n_p1 = log(abundance_estimate + 1),
  )

tmp2 <- tmp |>
  mutate(method = "All")

dfp <- bind_rows(tmp, tmp2)

plot_lambda_tp1 <- function(x, xlab) {
  a <- dfp |>
    ggplot() +
    aes(x = .data[[x]], y = lambda_tp1, color = method) +
    geom_smooth(alpha = 0.1) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(
      x = xlab,
      y = "Growth rate at time t + 1",
      color = "Method"
    ) +
    theme_bw()

  b <- dfp |>
    ggplot() +
    aes(x = .data[[x]], y = delta_lambda, color = method) +
    geom_smooth(alpha = 0.1) +
    # geom_point(alpha = 0.1) +
    # facet_grid(cols = vars(method)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(
      x = xlab,
      y = "Change in growth rate from time t to t + 1",
      color = "Method"
    ) +
    theme_bw()

  ggarrange(a, b, nrow = 1, common.legend = TRUE, legend = "right")
}

library(mgcv)

tmp_gam <- tmp |>
  filter(!is.na(percent_take)) |>
  mutate(
    c_lambda = (lambda - mean(lambda)) / sd(lambda),
    c_trap_count = (trap_count - mean(trap_count)) / sd(trap_count),
    c_effort = (effort - mean(effort)) / sd(effort),
    c_percent_take = (percent_take - mean(percent_take)) / sd(percent_take),
    c_take = (take - mean(take)) / sd(take),
    method = factor(method),
    st_name = factor(st_name)
  )

fit <- gam(
  lambda ~
    s(c_percent_take) +
    s(c_percent_take, c_trap_count) +
    s(log_take_p1) +
    s(c_effort) +
    s(c_trap_count) +
    s(method, bs = "re") +
    s(st_name, bs = "re"),
  method = "REML",
  data = tmp_gam
)

summary(fit)


k.check(fit)
gam.check(fit)
```

### Does removing more of a population change growth rate?

```         
x <- "percent_take"
xlab <- "Proportion removed at time t"
plot_lambda_tp1(x, xlab)
```
